the meaning of "Authenticator" is missing in the Glossary of Terms section.  I would also suggest adding it + the definition of Verifier to the Control Objective section as they are used often

the Glossary of Terms needs formatting

I think simplifying the wording in this section will make things easier for readers of the standard

2.1 "Verify authenticators are resistant to compromise, such as enforcing authentication decisions on a trusted device or service." NIST 5.2.7 talks about making the verifier resistant to compromise, not the authenticators.  Also, NIST 5.2.7 is only for AAL 3.  It isn't very clear what 2.1 addresses.  5.2.7 addresses ensuring that at least one authenticator is resistance to compromise when using MFA + you are at AAL 3

2.2 I think you meant verifiers, not authenticators "Verify authenticators CANNOT" -> "Verify verifiers CANNOT" 

and CANNOT should be changed to DO NOT

2.8 "... are secured by equivalent security controls." -> "are secured using equally strong security controls"

2.21 This requirement is a little ambiguous.  Is there any way to clear this up? Also, why does this point to NIST 5.1.1.1?

2.22 "The use of PSTN verifiers (such as SMS tokens) has been deprecated by NIST and SHOULD NOT be used."  Can you link to where this is stated?  As far as I can tell, 5.1.3.1 explicitly states that this is allowed: "The out-of-band authenticator SHALL uniquely authenticate itself in one of the following ways when communicating with the verifier: ...  Authenticate to a public mobile telephone network using a SIM card or equivalent that uniquely identifies the device. This method SHALL only be used if a secret is being sent from the verifier to the out-of-band device via the PSTN (SMS or voice)."

2.23 Authenticator -> verifier.  Is this needed for L1?  Also, in all cases, you'll probably want to add that you should lock it with the IP combination to prevent an attacker intentionally logging out users programmatically or other technique as mentioned here - https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#throttle  Also, this is quite similar to 2.20 so I'm not sure why it was added

2.26 Would things such as JWT refresh tokens and similar mechanisms considered as a form of re-authentication?  If not, then a lot of major sites don't even meet L1

2.27 I think you mean verifiers, not authenticators

2.29 I think that requiring the secrets management system to be resistant to offline attacks at L1 is excessive

2.32 I think this should be removed for L1

2.42 "complies uses with FIPS 140 approved algorithms and verification levels" -> "complies with FIPS 140 approved algorithms and verification levels"

2.45 "Verify the authentication system is compromise resistant, such as memorized secret breaches and/or client device reputation, and other controls."  This requirement is ambiguous.  I understand 5.2.7 but what is meant by "memorized secret breaches"?  I think it needs rewording

2.4x If you review NIST, this is for AAL2 and AAL3, not AAL1

2.47 This is a repeat of the rate limiting requirement mentioned in 2.20 + 2.23 or am I missing something?  If so, the same concerns mentioned above apply

2.48 "Verify memorized secret activation" I think this is ambiguous.  What is memorized secret activation

2.49 Ambiguous.  What is meant by being re-bound to a different identity?  And how would this be verified?
